subject: Follow-up: Dedicated pool sizing call — pick a slot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finnova.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finnova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated pool sizing call — pick a slot

Hi Daniel / Olivia —

Great conversation today — thanks for walking through Finnova's latency sensitivity and peak patterns. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the dedicated pool sizing call with our infra team: 

Recap (from discovery)
- Primary surface: customer-facing fraud scoring (+ some internal batch generation).
- Latency SLO: 95th < 200ms for score path; some background jobs can be higher.
- Expected steady qps: ~80–120 reqs/min (burst to ~300 reqs/min during batch runs).
- Typical payload size: ~350 tokens per request (includes metadata).

We'd like to schedule a 60-minute dedicated-capacity technical deep dive (engineers + SREs) to:
- Walk sample traffic (you) + load profile (we)
- Surface model variant / quantization options and expected throughput
- Define target concurrency and an initial GPU pool recommendation

Proposed slots (PT):
- Wed, Apr 21 — 10:00–11:00 AM PT
- Thu, Apr 22 — 2:00–3:00 PM PT

I've attached a short demo agenda and the traffic-profile template (traffic-profile.csv) — can you fill the CSV with a 1-hour sample or a representative peak window ahead of the call? That helps our infra team size the pool.

If neither slot works, send 2 alternatives that week and we'll prioritize overlap with our SREs.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: demo-agenda.pdf (1 page), traffic-profile.csv (template)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finnova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finnova.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated pool sizing call — pick a slot

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Thu Apr 22 2:00–3:00 PM PT works best for our team. Olivia (cc'd) will join from product and I'll loop in Sam (SRE) on the invite.

A couple of quick notes so your infra folks have context before the call:
- Average request size: ~320 tokens, but we see occasional instrumented traces hitting 800 tokens (long description + context).
- Typical concurrency today: 5–8 concurrent scoring calls, but target concurrency for steady-state is 10–15; batch window can push to 60 concurrent workers briefly.
- Our primary ask: predictable 95th latency (we can tolerate higher p99 for non-critical batch jobs).

I'll try to upload a 60-minute sample to the CSV by EOD Mon; if we can't get a full trace, we'll paste a minute-level summary.

One more: does Redwood require any special access for SREs to run an initial throughput test? We'd like to understand what logs or tokens you need so Sam can provision.

Best,
Daniel
Director, Platform Engineering | Finnova
Daniel.Park@finnova.com

[Inline: proposed slot confirmation — Thu Apr 22 2pm PT]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finnova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated pool sizing call — pick a slot

Thanks Daniel — confirmed on our side for Thu Apr 22, 2–3 PM PT. I'll be the SE running the throughput discussion and will bring our SRE lead (Sara L.) and a runtime engineer.

Pre-call checklist (short):
- If you can, attach a 10–15 minute sample trace or minute-level QPS vector in traffic-profile.csv. Even a CSV with timestamp + requests/min is fine.
- Share a representative prompt example (no PII) so we can estimate tokenization overhead.
- For throughput tests we typically ask for a non-prod API key with read-only ingestion that simulates traffic; if you can't provide that, we'll run tabletop sizing and provide pool recommendations.

Access/requirements for a basic throughput run:
- A short-lived API key (scope: inference:test) or a replayable request log (timestamped).
- Firewall rule to allow outbound to our test runner IP range (we'll share before the test).

I'll draft a calendar invite and include a secure link for uploading the CSV (or you can reply with the file).

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: none

Hi Daniel / Olivia —

Confirmed: Thu Apr 22, 2:00–3:00 PM PT — calendar invite sent (link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcd1234). Agenda below and a short pre-call checklist — please send what you can ahead of the call.

Agenda (60m)
- 0–10m: Introductions + goals (Finnova priorities)
- 10–25m: Walk traffic sample + concurrency patterns (Finnova)
- 25–40m: Runtime sizing recommendation (Redwood)
- 40–55m: Throughput test plan / timeline
- 55–60m: Next steps & mutual action items

Pre-call checklist
- Upload: traffic-profile.csv (1-hour sample or minute-level summary) — optional: anonymized sample request payloads
- Confirm: whether Sam can provision a short-lived test API key OR provide replay logs
- Optional: any compliance notes we should be aware of for a test run (IP allowlist, test data rules)

Attachments: precall-checklist.pdf (one-page with upload links and SRE contact info)

If helpful, Ben and I can run a 15-minute kickstart with Sam ahead of the deep dive just to align test credentials — let us know.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
